reason: The defect is real and I reproduced it exactly; the finding is refuted on its fix and on one of its own load-bearing measurements. VERIFIED TRUE: od -c on interaction-check.mjs:1231 and :1250 shows four 0x5C bytes in each escape (and grep for four-backslash sequences finds exactly those two lines in the whole gate, plus the same two lines at panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 and :115). Run under node with the bytes preserved by a file-editing tool, `re.source` is `\\bAugust\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})` — a literal backslash then b — `.test("finished in August, before")` is false, and the banned-vocabulary filter over "the callers accrues periods provider structured recorder" returns []. main innerText contains no backslash in any of the four states (checked), so `found` and `hits` are structurally empty and eight assertions (`no month is named without its year` and `the refusals speak the reader's language`, each x full/partial/quiet/first-run) cannot fail. That much stands, and it is the class the round notes say is worth the most. VERIFIED FALSE: the finding's claim that it re-ran the same two checks with single escapes against the live surface and got 'bareMonths []' in all four states. Driven in chromium at 1440, reducedMotion, ?v=light&state=<state>, with `new RegExp("\\b" + m + "\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})", "g")` — i.e. the finding's own proposed line 1231 verbatim — bareMonths is ["May"] in full, partial AND quiet. The hit is the chart's screen-reader description: "twelve weeks of finished work, week commencing 27 Apr to 13 Jul: 27 Apr, 5; 4 May, 3; 11 May, 6; 18 May, 4; 25 May, 7; 1 Jun, 5; ...". May is the one month whose abbreviation equals its full name, so the month list matches the short-form date labels; Apr/Jun/Jul do not collide and first-run has no such strip, which is why first-run alone comes back []. So the proposed fix does not restore a green gate — it turns three of the eight assertions red on a correct, frozen surface, in the closing round, on a false positive (a day-and-month inside an explicitly bounded, explicitly dated range is not the bare month in prose that august-inside-a-july-reading was about). A fix that makes the measured baseline red is worse than the vacuity it replaces, and it fails its own stated standard of proof: the seat reports a measurement it evidently did not get. The banned-vocabulary half of the fix (line 1250 / :115) is correct as written — with two backslashes, hits is [] in all four states. Severity is not overstated: defect is right. Nothing on the product surface is wrong — driven, no month is named without its year in prose, no studio vocabulary survives, the only year-bearing strings are "June 2027" and (first-run) "August 2026" — so this is a dead instrument, not a product that asserts something untrue. L-05 does bite on the record: those two round-1 closures currently rest on checks that cannot fail, and the 461-green count is overstating coverage by eight until the corrected lines land.
sharpenedFix: Two edits per file, with a file-editing tool, never through a heredoc (this environment's shell halves backslashes in a quoted heredoc — I confirmed it while reproducing this). (1) interaction-check.mjs:1250 and panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:115: `const hits = banned.filter((w) => new RegExp("\\b" + w + "\\b", "i").test(text));` — two source backslashes each; verified green in all four states. (2) interaction-check.mjs:1231 and panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 need two backslashes AND a guard against the short-form date labels, or they go red on "4 May": `const re = new RegExp("(?<!\\d\\s)\\b" + m + "\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})", "g");` — a month immediately preceded by a day-of-month number is a date, not a bare month. Driven at 1440 in all four states this returns [] on the live surface, and appending "finished in August, before the week is out" to the page text makes it return ["August"] in every state, so it still catches the exact regression it was written for. Add a third `ok()` beside them asserting the instrument itself is alive — e.g. that the same regex applied to a fixed literal probe string returns the expected hit — so this class cannot recur silently in either direction. Then re-run the full gate and re-state its assertion count.
breaks: The seat's fix as written breaks the measured baseline: three assertions (`no month is named without its year` for full, partial, quiet) go red immediately on "4 May"/"11 May"/"18 May"/"25 May" in the chart's sr-only description, so `interaction-check.mjs` — one of the two gates the brief calls green — exits non-zero on a surface that is correct. Anyone applying it in the closing round would then be pushed toward the wrong remedy: changing the chart's accessible date labels to satisfy a bad check, which would damage the screen-reader reading of a protected object. With the sharpened form, the lookbehind narrows the check, so re-measure: (a) the full gate green and its true assertion count restated (currently reported as 461; 133 `ok(` call sites, eight of the emitted assertions vacuous today); (b) the negative control above, proving the regex fires on an injected bare month in each of the four states; (c) that the guard is not too wide — confirm a genuine prose regression like "back in August" (no leading digit) still trips it, which it does; (d) the banned-vocabulary check re-run in all four states after the escape fix (green when I ran it). Lookbehind is fine in chromium, so no engine risk. Nothing on the rendered surface changes, so no shots, contrast or layout need re-capturing.
